cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Joy – a feeling of great pleasure and happiness.

p.em: Example: The campy anthem celebrates pure joy and uninhibited fun.

cosy-blockquote.p: Anticipation – the action of anticipating something; expectation.

p.em: Example: The countdown created electric anticipation on the dance floor.

cosy-blockquote.p: Abundance – a very large quantity of something.

p.em: Example: The song humorously predicts an abundance of handsome suitors.

cosy-blockquote.p: Euphoria – a feeling or state of intense excitement and happiness.

p.em: Example: The high-energy chorus fills the room with infectious euphoria.

cosy-blockquote.p: Celebration – the action of marking an important event or occasion.

p.em: Example: Singing this disco classic turns any night into a party celebration.
Example: The listeners expressed sheer delight as the beat dropped.

cosy-blockquote.p: Energy – the strength and vitality required for sustained activity.

p.em: Example: The Weather Girls deliver powerful vocal energy throughout.

cosy-blockquote.p: Fellowship – friendly association, especially with people who share interests.

p.em: Example: Dancing together builds a joyful sense of fellowship.

cosy-blockquote.p: Warmth – enthusiasm, affection, or physical heat.

p.em: Example: The song brings humor and warmth to everyone on the floor.

cosy-blockquote.p: Sensation – a widespread reaction of interest and excitement.

p.em: Example: When released in 1982, the hit became a worldwide dance sensation.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Share whether you agree or disagree with these statements and discuss them with your teacher:

ul.li: Incorrect: It is raining men → Correct: It will rain ((Use 'going to' for predictions based on present evidence.))
Incorrect: Humidity is rising up → Correct: Humidity is rising ((Avoid redundant prepositions; 'rise' already implies upward motion.))
Incorrect: Listen the → Correct: Listen to ((Always use preposition 'to' after 'listen' when specifying an object.))
